how: Read from evidence/STRATEGY_IDEAS_INPUT.json, which tools/strategy_ideas.py extracted from each canonical file (docstring, settings, indicator calls, entry/exit conditions, method inventory), plus a direct read of the files whose conditions are built in helper variables, plus user_data/family_deltas.py for the version-to-version notes: it compares consecutive revisions of a family and prints settings changes, added and removed indicator calls and methods, the changed conditions and the size. Every sentence names the code fact it rests on in `evidence`. Each family names the one revision it was read from in `read_from`, with that revision's source_sha256; tools/strategy_ideas.py --check compares it against the corpus and the page marks it stale when the corpus has moved on. The family's other strategies are derived from the corpus by stem, so nothing here lists 39 hashes to say what the corpus already knows.
scope: forty-eight families in three batches. Batch 1: the ten the published family table leads with (Zaratustra, Slope, RSIBB, EMA + Fibonacci, el_extrema, Rsiqui, BollingerMACD, GnF, EWOist, PlusMinus). Batches 2 and 3: the thirty-nine largest stems in the corpus by number of strategies, ranks 1 to 39 of `python -m tools.strategy_ideas --rank`, which is why E0V1E, Ichimoku and the other large stems are here. Zaratustra and Rsiqui appear in two of the batches and are written once. The corpus holds about 2,000 stems, so this is a sample chosen by one stated rule, not a survey.
